Runtime counter intervals are reported when available; release cadence and human gameplay acceptance remain separate.

Paired serial intervals use conservative UTC fences from journal-matched debug replies and exclude the first classified departure/error/exit or marked quit. Firmware uptimes are local to each device and are never synchronized by assumption. Sparse or rejected anchors can leave paired duration unproven despite increasing local counters.
Memory lines are informational snapshots, not allocation-failure proof. STARTUP_FAILED and LOADING_FAILED are failure receipts even when firmware logs them at INFO severity.

GCAWAIT loading keepalives prove neither engine readiness nor simulation progress; the current firmware does not emit a serial receipt for every keepalive. Their absence from text logs is not proof of absent transport traffic.

Screenshot transport receipts bind raw RGB565 bytes separately from the PNG file hash. Captured frames require image inspection before visual acceptance; capture alone does not prove a person saw the panel.
Request duration includes client work, holds and waits; a screenshot also includes transfer and encoding. Both-unit commands run sequentially, so the total is not per-unit UI latency.
Peer departure is claimed only where a PLAYER_LEFT receipt is present; quit commands alone are not graceful-exit proof.
The last debug response is the last received reply, which may predate a later engine load, error or reboot; shell-ready serial receipts and boot versions are recorded separately.
